text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and the language is cautious, but the summary is internally conflicted and generic. The headline says 'too few returned records to judge' while 29 records came back and 10 of them were 99215 claims, all supported at the billed level. The 'inconclusive' leaning is defensible, but it does not weigh the strong billing-pattern signal (7.27x expected, z=3.68) against the documentation that supports the billed level. The summary also leaves out the complexity gradient showing 99215 rises with conditions.","problems":["Headline 'too few returned records' is unclear and arguably contradicts the body: 29 charts returned, 10 of them 99215, none below billed level.","Does not reconcile the strong statistical outlier signal with documentation that fully supports the billed level, so the investigator has to redo that analysis.","Only two example claims are cited, both from the low-complexity set. Documented 99215 claims that were supported (e.g. C0000113) are not cited, and the cited claims are not documented ones, so the examples don't tie to the documentation finding.","The next step to request a 'targeted sample' of 99215 charts starting with C0000026 and C0000055 is somewhat generic; it does not say how many charts to request or why those two, and the chosen claims have no returned documentation.","Omits that the 99215 rate rises with complexity (15% at 0 conditions to 65% at 5+), which supports the sicker-panel explanation, and does not mention the one 99215 note with minutes 'not recorded'."]}
